summary: The way a web page reaches a headset or a phone's pass-through camera: it covers starting and ending an immersive session, the tracked spaces, the viewer's pose, the views to draw, the input sources and the frame loop. It is not finished. The core document is a Candidate Recommendation Draft dated 9 June 2026, and no part of this family has ever reached full Recommendation, so nobody should describe it as a completed web standard. Read it as a core plus a fan of modules that sit at very different stages: only the augmented reality module has reached candidate stage alongside the core, seven more are Working Drafts, and the anchors, plane detection and graphics binding documents are editor's drafts that have never been published on the technical reports track at all. It draws nothing itself and binds only to the older web graphics interface; the document that would let it use the newer one is one of those unpublished editor's drafts. Two traps for a standards audience: anchors can be made to survive a restart on the same device and the same site, but there is no way to share one with another device or another person and the word share does not appear in the anchors document at all, and there is no eye tracking module of any kind, so the gaze value in the core is head direction rather than eye direction.

coverage.note: It draws nothing. It hands the page a framebuffer and a frame callback, and the drawing is done with the web graphics interface.
